title: Protocols for Collecting Mouse PDL Cells and Bone Marrow Cells
author: Sirisereephap, Surboyo, et al.
materials: SCBM stromal cell growth basal medium
SCGM stromal cell growth medium SingleQuots

steps.title: Sterilize surgical instruments
steps.instruction: Autoclave the following tools at 121 °C for 20 min the day before mouse sacrifice: 26G needle, 1 mL syringe, no. 10 scalpel blade, curved forceps (Perry), suture‑tying forceps, Dumont forceps, and surgical scissors.

steps.title: Prepare PDL complete medium
steps.instruction: On the day of sacrifice, set a water bath with agitation to 37 °C, 200 rpm and pre‑chill the centrifuge to 4 °C. Prepare the PDL complete medium, filter it through a 0.22 µm polyether‑sulfone (PES) membrane, and equilibrate to room temperature for 1 h before use.

steps.title: Prepare PDL digestion buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the PDL digestion buffer freshly on the day of sacrifice, filter it through a 0.22 µm PES membrane, and equilibrate to room temperature for 1 h before use.

steps.title: Prepare PDLC subculture reagents
steps.instruction: Pre‑chill the centrifuge to 4 °C, prepare PDL complete media (filter through 0.22 µm PES, equilibrate 1 h at room temperature), and thaw the ReagentPack Subculture Reagents stored at –20 °C, allowing them to equilibrate to room temperature for 1 h (optional: pre‑thaw at 4 °C for 2 days to shorten equilibration).

steps.title: Prepare osteogenic differentiation medium
steps.instruction: Prepare osteogenic differentiation medium (ODM), filter through a 0.22 µm PES membrane, and equilibrate to room temperature for 1 h before use; prepare fresh ODM weekly to ensure consistent differentiation results.

steps.title: Prepare osteoclast supplemental medium
steps.instruction: Pre‑chill the centrifuge to 4 °C, prepare the osteoclast supplemental medium, filter through a 0.22 µm PES membrane, and equilibrate to room temperature for 30 min before use.

steps.title: Prepare osteoclast differentiation medium
steps.instruction: Prepare the osteoclast differentiation medium, filter through a 0.22 µm PES membrane, and equilibrate to room temperature for 30 min before use.

steps.title: Alizarin Red S staining
steps.instruction: Stain osteogenically differentiated cultures with Alizarin Red S after 28 days using a 48‑well plate (adjust volume for other plate formats).

substeps.instruction: Prepare 2 % Alizarin Red S solution: dissolve 1 g Alizarin Red S in 50 mL ddH₂O, vortex 30 s, prepare 0.2 M NH₄OH in ddH₂O, adjust the solution pH to 6.3–6.4 with the NH₄OH, filter through a 0.22 µm membrane, and store at 4 °C protected from light for up to one month.
Aspirate the osteogenic differentiation medium from each well.
Add 0.2 mL DPBS (no calcium, no magnesium) to each well to wash the cells.
Fix the cells with 0.2 mL 10 % formalin, incubate 1 h at room temperature, then remove formalin with a pipette (avoid touching the well bottom). Wash the cells twice with 0.2 mL ddH₂O.
Add 0.2 mL freshly made Alizarin Red S solution (pH 6.3–6.4) to each well and incubate in the dark for 45 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the Alizarin Red S solution and wash the cells twice with 0.2 mL ddH₂O.
For histological images: carefully aspirate the wash buffer, add 0.2 mL DPBS (no calcium, no magnesium) per well, then capture images using a stereo microscope.

For stereological images: aspirate any remaining liquid, dry the plate overnight at room temperature, photograph the wells with a Leica EZ4 Stereo Microscope, analyze the ARS‑positive area with ImageJ, and compare the results to control samples using Prism software.

description: The current study showing great potential to find the treatment in periodontitis is the exploration of regenerative medicine, or therapeutic agents having the capacity to promote osteogenic differentiation, to promote bone growth in a bone defect area. This involves utilizing stem cells or PDL cells to investigate how drugs can stimulate the differentiation of those cells into cells at the later stage of development, such as osteoblasts that are responsible for new bone formation.2 Osteogenic differentiation is the transformation of undifferentiated cells, such as mesenchymal stem cells and PDLCs, into osteoblasts, which plays a pivotal role in bone formation. PDLCs, cells derived from the periodontium that encompasses and supports the teeth, have the ability to undergo osteogenic differentiation when exposed to specific conditions.3 This process typically involves subjecting PDLCs to an osteogenic medium containing components such as dexamethasone, β-glycerophosphate, and ascorbic acid. These components replicate the biochemical environment necessary for the development of osteoblasts. Throughout the osteogenic differentiation process, PDLCs adopt osteoblastic characteristics, including the synthesis of extracellular matrix proteins, such as collagen, and the formation of mineralized nodules.4 In addition to investigating therapeutic drugs for their impact on osteogenic differentiation, the examination the drugs effect on osteoclasts offers an avenue to explore the inhibitory effects on osteoclastogenesis, thereby impeding bone loss during the progression of periodontitis.5 Osteoclastogenesis refers to the formation of osteoclasts, cells responsible for bone resorption. In in vitro studies focusing on osteoclastogenesis, the primary goal is usually to understand the factors and mechanisms influencing the differentiation and maturation of osteoclasts. Anticipated outcomes may differ based on distinct experimental conditions, cell types used, and the study objectives
